description:
KFT 0.7.0's two audio `modality` rows — the half of the pickup that is koine's own (AUD-6), and the third row a named consumer has now asked for.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TEXT (2026-09-12, before this tasklist was authored).

AUD-6 HOLDS. `grep -rli 'text-to-audio\|audio-to-audio' scenarios/` returns NOTHING: none of the twelve pressure tests walks an audio job. `e2e-finetune-multimodal.md` — the fully-multimodal KFT leg — contains the string 'audio' zero times; it walks `image-text-to-text` and `text-to-video`. So KFT §3.1's two audio rows are UNEXERCISED VOCABULARY: no KCS encoding can assert one, and neither row is citable in a re-ratification. Four of the six AUD findings are discharged downstream and the fifth is deferred and owned there; AUD-6 is the only one that is koine's, and the scenario plus its encoding are the join neither side can author alone.

THE THIRD ROW, AND THE TRIGGER THAT FIRED. `docs/reference/generative-audio-modalities.md` §4 declines `audio-text-to-text` and states its own reversal condition in terms: 'Audio *understanding* — transcription, captioning, audio QA — is the fourth member of the `…-text-to-text` family and IS A GENUINE GAP. It is not minted here because NOTHING HAS ASKED FOR IT … a row is worth contracting when a named provider needs the vocabulary. THE TRIGGER: THE FIRST CONSUMER THAT DOES.' A specialized local-only fine-tuning provider has now asked, in a written proposal dated 2026-08-25 held in its own tree, for `audio-text-to-text` on §3.1 at `lora`/`qlora` — with `sft` deliberately not requested, since both of its backends implement LoRA SFT — carrying a capability probe, a tested audio processor, a declared memory profile and an Apache-2.0 anchored base already committed behind a row it cannot reach. NO FILE IN THIS REPO CITES THAT PROPOSAL: `grep -rn 'koine-audio-modality-proposal'` matches only the roadmap row that records the ask. So the first thing this tasklist owes is a record that the proposal exists and was read.

RATIFYING IS KOINE'S ACT; ADOPTING IS THE PROVIDER'S. Until koine answers, an audio-understanding job there is refused `unknown-modality` at the VOCABULARY gate — which runs before the placement gate, the base anchor and the probe — so the refusal blocks that whole arm rather than one combination. That is why this is categorised `unblock`: its value is releasing work that is otherwise stopped, in one repo by a missing scenario and in another by a missing token.

FOUR STATEMENTS OF ONE ENUM. If the row is ratified it is not one edit: `registry/enums/modality.tsv` is the registry statement, KFT §3.1's table is the prose statement, `schemas/finetune-job.schema.json` carries the enum inline (seven tokens today), and `registry/entity-types.tsv` points the `model` entity's `modality` refinement at the registry file. §3.1's own discipline binds the decision either way: the vocabulary is CLOSED and ADDITIVE, a new modality 'adds a row plus a capability variant (§2), never a new plane', and the tokens are IMMUTABLE once published — a change is a new token, never an edit in place. So minting is cheap and unminting is not, which is the asymmetry the decision must be taken against.

userStories.title: A pressure leg that walks an audio job, so the two rows stop being unexercised vocabulary
userStories.description: AUD-6, and it is koine's half. Without a scenario, `text-to-audio` and `audio-to-audio` are tokens no re-ratification can cite.
acceptanceCriteria: A pressure leg exists under `scenarios/` that walks an audio finetune job end to end, exercising BOTH rows — `text-to-audio` (caption→audio, the third row of the `text-to-image`/`text-to-video` family) and `audio-to-audio` (paired asset↔asset with NO caption side, which is the distinction §3.1 argues at length and the one a leg must actually put pressure on).

It is adversarial in the house style — it prefers finding breaks over asserting correctness, tags every step held or broke, and files each break as a numbered delta. A leg that returns clean because it avoided the hard seams is not a pass.

It exercises what §3.1 claims moves NO clause of §4: that both sides of an audio pair are `dataset.media[]` entries, so §4.2's effective-egress union over every media asset and §4.3's license/trust union already reach them. That claim is checked against §4's text by the walk rather than restated.

The leg is added to `scenarios/README.md`'s table with its pressure-tested sections, what it hunts, its deltas and its KCS-encoding column — the index is how a scenario is reachable, and `check-doc-integrity.mjs` enforces that every relative link resolves.

AUD-6 is updated in `docs/reference/generative-audio-modalities-downstream.md` to record what now exercises the rows and what remains — in particular that the machine-replayable encoding of this leg is downstream work, not koine's.

userStories.title: Answer the `audio-text-to-text` ask — against koine's own stated trigger
userStories.description: koine declined the row in advance and published the condition that reverses the decline. A named consumer now needs the vocabulary. Record the reading and the verdict.
acceptanceCriteria: The proposal is CITED in this repo for the first time — who asked, when (dated 2026-08-25), what exactly was asked for (`audio-text-to-text` on §3.1 at `lora`/`qlora`, with `sft` deliberately not requested), and what stands behind it (a capability probe, a tested audio processor, a declared memory profile, an Apache-2.0 anchored base). Refer to the asker BY ROLE, never by repository or product name: this repo is public and its rows are role-scoped and product-agnostic by design.

The published trigger in `docs/reference/generative-audio-modalities.md` §4 is quoted and applied: *'nothing has asked for it … The trigger: the first consumer that does.'* The verdict states whether the trigger has fired and follows from that reading rather than from preference.

The verdict is recorded either way, in the same document that declined the row, so a later reader sees the decline and its answer in one place. §5's forward-declaration standard — a row is worth contracting when a named provider needs the vocabulary — is the standard actually applied.

The asymmetry §3.1 states is weighed on the record: the vocabulary is closed and additive, a new modality adds a row plus a capability variant and never a new plane, and tokens are IMMUTABLE once published — splitting later is additive and cheap, unsplitting is not.
GATES: koine's six checks green, with observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: VERDICT: RATIFY. Recorded as a new §7 of docs/reference/generative-audio-modalities.md — the same document that declined the row — plus a forward pointer appended to §4's declining bullet (left standing as the dated record) and a second up-front verdict paragraph. Proposal CITED for the first time in this repo (verified before writing: `grep -rn 'koine-audio-modality-proposal'` matched exactly ONE line, ROADMAP's row, and no spec, registry, schema or reference page): asker by ROLE only — the specialized `finetune` provider role, the narrow local-only trainer for containment-gated synthetic/personal data (ECOSYSTEM §2) — never by repository or product; dated 2026-08-25; ask = `audio-text-to-text` on §3.1 at `lora`/`qlora` with `sft` deliberately not requested (both backends implement LoRA SFT); behind it a capability probe, a tested audio processor, a declared memory profile and an Apache-2.0 anchored base already committed. TRIGGER QUOTED VERBATIM and applied clause by clause: 'nothing has asked for it' FALSE now; 'no participant in ECOSYSTEM §2 is waiting on it' FALSE now (asker holds a §2 role, the same one §5's table already records as waiting on `audio-to-audio`); §5's standard 'a named provider needs the vocabulary' MET and over-met — so the verdict follows from the reading. Also recorded that the trigger does NOT condition on an implementation existing (§5 contracts ahead of providers on purpose), so the probe/base are corroboration, not the qualification — a trigger that gains conditions on the day it fires is not a trigger. The row was then checked against the columns §3.1 carries rather than admitted on the trigger alone: no new plane (knowledge + media(KMI audio)); differs from image-/video-text-to-text on port + typical base and from text-to-audio/audio-to-audio on port; without it FT-F validates a false declaration or the whole arm is refused `unknown-modality` at the vocabulary gate (which runs before placement, base anchor and probe); and NO §4 clause moves — checked against §4's text per AU-2's lesson — because its asset+text corpus is exactly FT-I's named shape, the side of §4.1 that carries. One consequence recorded rather than left to be found: FT-I's bullet ENUMERATES its members, so a third `…-text-to-text` row widens AU-1's fold from two rows to three — same sentence, same defect, no new delta. ASYMMETRY WEIGHED ON THE RECORD (§7.4): closed + additive + tokens immutable once published, so minting is cheap and unminting impossible — the question is the GRAIN, decided as one token covering transcription/captioning/audio-QA (the grain image-text-to-text and text-to-audio already use), with §4's `text-to-speech` split condition restated for it so the next reader meets a condition rather than a silence. LANDING IS A SEPARATE ACT and is US-3's: no token moved, no version moved, no clause moved — `git diff --stat` is 2 files, specs/ and registry/ and schemas/ untouched. userStories.title: If the row is ratified, every statement of the enum moves together
userStories.description: One token, four places. A validator on a stale enum rejects a conformant job, which is the exact failure the 0.7.0 pickup was written to prevent.
acceptanceCriteria: If US-2's verdict is to RATIFY: the token lands in EVERY statement of the enum in this repo, in file order, with the data-plane port, typical base and typical `method` columns filled — `registry/enums/modality.tsv`, KFT §3.1's table, and the inline `modality` enum in `schemas/finetune-job.schema.json`; `registry/entity-types.tsv`'s `model` refinement pointer is checked to still resolve. A grep proving no statement was missed is recorded, not asserted.

The `modality × method` pairing is stated as asked and as decided — the admission check under FT-F validates the combination and rejects an incompatible request with a report before any compute is committed, so a row whose methods are wrong makes that check validate a false declaration.

If US-2's verdict is to DECLINE: no file is edited except the record of the decision and the trigger, restated so the next asker meets a condition rather than a silence. This story is satisfied by either verdict, provided the verdict was reached in US-2 and the record says which.

The KFT version move follows §3.1's additive discipline and is recorded with reasoning; if it moves, all three status mirrors (`README.md`, `specs/README.md`, `ECOSYSTEM.md`) move with it, which `check-doc-integrity.mjs` enforces. The downstream notice is updated so mirrors know which of koine's statements to vendor from.

`node scripts/check-schemas.mjs` and `node scripts/check-registry.mjs` are both green over the edited enum and TSV, with the observed row counts recorded (today: 7 modality rows, 29 relation names, 9 schemas).
